overview: Webhooks / HTTP Requests uses API key authentication. You generate an API key in your Webhooks / HTTP Requests account settings and pass it with every API request. No OAuth flow is required — the key identifies and authenticates your application directly.

steps.title: Log in to your Webhooks / HTTP Requests account
steps.description: Sign in to your Webhooks / HTTP Requests account and navigate to the API or developer settings section. This is usually found under Account → Settings → API or Developer Settings.

steps.title: Find your API credentials
steps.description:
Locate the following credentials in the Webhooks / HTTP Requests settings:

• **Authorization Header Value** (`apiKey`) — Optional: value to send as Authorization header (e.g., 'Bearer token123' or 'Basic abc==')
steps.tip: Copy the credentials immediately — some keys are shown only once.
steps.warning: Never share your API key publicly or commit it to source control.

steps.title: Create the connection
steps.tip: Use a unique connection_id per user or account to support multiple connections.

apiKey.label: Authorization Header Value
apiKey.description: Optional: value to send as Authorization header (e.g., 'Bearer token123' or 'Basic abc==')

tips: Store your API key in environment variables — never hardcode it.
If your key is compromised, regenerate it immediately from the Webhooks / HTTP Requests settings.
